message.content:
Based on my investigation, I've identified the root cause of the performance issue.

The `missing_space_before_subcommand` rule (`thefuck/rules/missing_space_before_subcommand.py`) relies on `get_all_executables()` (from `thefuck/utils.py`), which scans *every* directory in `PATH` and lists all their contents (`Path(path).iterdir()`). On WSL2, `PATH` includes slow DrvFS-mounted Windows directories (e.g. `/mnt/c/...`), so this full scan takes ~8 seconds every time thefuck runs (a fresh process each invocation, so the in-memory `memoize` doesn't help).

The fix is to rewrite the rule so it doesn't trigger the expensive full-PATH directory scan. Instead of iterating over all executables looking for a prefix match, it can iterate over the prefixes of the first script part (longest first) and use the fast `which()` lookup (a direct per-path file check, no directory listing) to find e.g. `git` in `gitbranch`. This removes the dependency on `get_all_executables()` from this rule entirely — the change belongs in the rule file.
